02 / The part nobody told him

Kegels were never just for women.

The same hidden muscle group women learn about after pregnancy also supports a man's bladder, bowel, core coordination, and sexual function.

01

He has the same basic training need.

Squeeze, hold, fully release, and build control over time. The hard part is knowing what to do and staying consistent.

02

Problems do not have to come first.

Pelvic floor training can be a private strength habit—not a reaction to embarrassment or a diagnosis.

03 / Why you may both care

Benefits for him. A difference you may share.

No hype and no promises. Just the practical reasons pelvic floor strength and control can matter inside—and outside—your relationship.

For himDirect benefits
  • Better bladder controlTraining may help with leakage, urgency, and the drips that can follow a bathroom visit.
  • Support for sexual functionThe male pelvic floor affects erections and ejaculatory control. Better coordination may improve confidence and performance.
  • A stronger foundationThese muscles support the bladder and bowel and work with the rest of the core during lifting, coughing, and daily movement.
For both of youShared impact
  • More confidence, less avoidanceFeeling more in control can reduce self-consciousness around everyday life and intimacy.
  • More intentional intimacyImproved strength and control may support a better experience for him—and that can matter to both partners.
  • A healthy habit you can shareYou can both use the app, train privately, and compare consistency without turning it into an awkward conversation.

Results vary. Pelvic floor exercises are not right for everyone; pain, difficulty urinating, or persistent symptoms should be discussed with a qualified health professional.
